title: Method of successive approximations for solving integral equations of actuarial mathematics
summary: The dissertation considers various generalizations of the classical risk process describing the stochastic evolution of the capital of an insurance company (Cramer Lundberg model), including processes with variable deterministic or random premiums, non Poisson flows of premiums and claims, and a stochastic Markovian environment. Integral equations for the probability of nonruin as a function of initial capital are derived for these generalizations.
